newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money rises, offshore unload papers.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money rises, offshore unload papers.

text.p: Jakarta call money rose to 18.0 percent from 11.5/12.0 percent on Friday, while foreign players were seen unloading medium-term papers, dealers said.
They said bond prices were stable on local support.
Dealers said overnight liquidity was tight despite an injection from the central bank of 1.524 trillion rupiah.
They said month-end and weekend factors, together with the weekly tax payments due Friday, seemed to have caused operators to hold back from offering.

"I don't think the market is really tight. It's just the perception which makes the market nervous," one dealer said. He said sharp rises in short-dated swaps seemed to have lifted short-term money to higher levels.
Overnight swaps rose to 3.5/4.0 and tom/next to 1.4 points.
Longer-term rates were edging higher following rises in short- and longer-term swaps. One-month money was at 13.375 percent and three-month at 13.75/14.00 percent, respectively.

The central bank kept its rates for bilateral papers (SBIs) stable on Friday. It offered 3-5 day SBIs at eight percent, seven-day at nine percent, 14-day at 10.0 percent, 21-day at 10.5 percent, one- and three-month at 11.25 and 12.00 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Thursday was 12.49 percent, compared with 12.36 percent on Wednesday.
Bond dealers said prices were stable, but offshore players appeared to be rather nervous following Thursday's riot in a small town east of Jakarta.
They said early unfounded rumours of trouble in other towns made offshore players nervous, triggering some unloading in high-yielding medium-term notes.
"It's difficult to convince them that we have no trouble in Jakarta or elsewhere. There is no threat to our national stability, but they just want to cut losses for now," one said.
But the dealer said bond prices remained stable on the back of strong support from local institutions.
Dealers said the yield of the benchmark PLN V/A bond was steady at 15.37 percent at the price of 105.25 percent.
They said the grey market price of the five-year 400 billion rupiah straight bonds of PT Astra International remained at 100.25 percent.
